questions.prompt: How should the primary layout be organized for the NLP UX?
questions.description: Currently, it uses a left sidebar for Notebooks/Commands and a right main area.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Three-pane design: Document tree sidebar (left), Results/Query list (top-right), Selected document/answer detail (bottom-right), with a query input at the bottom.

options.label: Three-pane: Tree sidebar, Results list, Selected document detail
Two-pane: Document tree sidebar, Main results area, Bottom query input

questions.prompt: How should we display NLP processing (embedding, indexing, retrieving)?
questions.description: Rich offers several ways to show live feedback as demonstrated in the examples.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Use a multi-task Progress bar in a dedicated footer or overlay for pipeline stages.

options.label: Multi-task Progress bar in the footer
Status spinner next to the query input
Dedicated logging panel showing live pipeline events

questions.prompt: How should search results and NLP responses be formatted?
questions.description: Rich provides Markdown, Syntax highlighting, and Tables.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Rich Table with score columns, combined with Markdown/Syntax highlighting for text snippets.

options.label: Markdown for generated answers and document content
Tree view for document hierarchy and semantic clustering

questions.prompt: How will the user input queries or commands?
questions.description: The current TUI uses raw single-keypress tracking. Text input requires special handling.
questions.recommendedAnswer: A dedicated input bar at the bottom that activates an input mode to accept text (like Vim/Helix command mode).

options.label: Dedicated bottom input bar activated by a keypress (e.g. '/')
Popup prompt overlay using rich Prompt.ask
